raw_answer_text:
Looking at the validation errors, the issue is with how elements are declared in the flowchart genre. The current syntax `process checkcounters "label"` is being rejected. 

Since I don't have access to the `reference/experimental/flowchart.md` file that documents the flowchart genre specifically, but the error indicates the ID placement is the problem, I'll try inverting the order to place the ID before the type keyword. This is consistent with how many similar languages work.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "BGP session reset procedure"

checkcounters process "Check interface error counters"
errorsfound decision "Errors found?"
clearcounters process "Clear interface counters"
monitor terminator "Monitor session"
escalate terminator "Escalate to operator"

checkcounters -> errorsfound
errorsfound yes -> clearcounters
clearcounters -> monitor
errorsfound no -> escalate
```

The key change from the prior attempt: element declarations now follow the pattern `id type "label"` instead of `type id "label"`. This moves the identifier before the type keyword, which should resolve the "not allowed" validation errors on the element declarations.
